title: RIGL: A Unified Reciprocal Approach for Tracing the Independent and Group Learning Processes

problem.claim: The work addresses tracing students' knowledge states across independent and group learning processes.

gap.claim: Existing approaches mainly model independent learning, while group learning and the reciprocal effects between the two processes remain insufficiently explored.

contributions.claim: RIGL is a unified reciprocal model for tracing knowledge states at individual and group levels.
The model includes a time frame-aware reciprocal embedding module and reciprocal enhanced learning modeling to represent student-group interactions and complementary behavioral information.
The model includes a relation-guided temporal attentive network with dynamic graph modeling and temporal self-attention, plus a bias-aware contrastive learning module.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on four real-world educational datasets demonstrating the effectiveness of RIGL.
The authors report that the code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Independent and group learning are presented as established educational paradigms, with different learning directions.
Deep temporal models have been used to trace knowledge-state dynamics in intelligent education.
Prior work emphasizes independent learning and insufficiently studies group learning and reciprocal effects between the two processes.
RIGL combines reciprocal embeddings, enhanced learning modeling, relation-guided temporal attention, dynamic graph modeling, temporal self-attention, and bias-aware contrastive learning.
The authors report effectiveness on four real-world educational datasets and make the code available.

source_observation.claim: The paper models individual and group learning jointly and uses reciprocal information between them.

interpretation.claim: When related behavioral processes may influence one another, a joint model can represent complementary information that separate models may miss.

application.claim: Consider reciprocal or multi-level modeling when analyzing systems containing individual and group interactions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that reciprocal modeling is beneficial outside the reported educational setting or datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the four datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, ablations, computational costs, or limitations.
